title: Finite saturation of a fine monoid and localization compatibility
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral commutative monoid, written additively; integral means that $P$ embeds in its group completion $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Define
$$P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{g\in G:\text{there is }n\geq1\text{ with }ng\in P\}.$$
Then $P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is a finitely generated integral saturated monoid, its group completion is $G$, and there is a finite subset $F\subset P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ with
$$P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P).$$
For any submonoid $S\subseteq P$, write $P-S=\{p-s:p\in P,\ s\in S\}\subseteq G$. Saturation commutes with localization:
$$(P-S)^{\mathrm{sat}}=P^{\mathrm{sat}}-S\quad\text{inside }G.$$
Here and in the equality the saturation is taken in $G$. For a commutative ring $R$ and a monoid $T$, write $R[T]=\bigoplus_{t\in T}Rz^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. Then $R[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is a finite $R[P]$-module, meaning that it is generated as an $R[P]$-module by finitely many elements. No torsion-freeness assumption on $G$ is made.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101 (saturation and compatibility with localization); 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104, finiteness of the toric saturation morphism. Only the finiteness assertion is used, not the normalization assertion.

proof.text: Choose generators $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of $P$; their classes generate $G$, so $G$ is a finitely generated abelian group. Let $T$ be its torsion subgroup and $L=G/T$ with projection $\pi:G\to L$, $\overline g=\pi(g)$. The group $L$ is finitely generated, and torsion-free: if $k\overline g=0$ with $k>0$ then $kg\in T$, so $g\in T$. By [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free], $L$ has a finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$. Choosing $\tilde e_j\in G$ with $\pi(\tilde e_j)=e_j$, the map $L\to G$, $e_j\mapsto\tilde e_j$, is a section of $\pi$, so $G=T\oplus\tilde L$ and $T$ is a quotient of $G$, hence finitely generated; a finitely generated torsion abelian group with generators $t_1,\ldots,t_k$ of orders $m_1,\ldots,m_k$ has at most $m_1\cdots m_k$ elements, so $T$ is finite, of order $m$ say. Apply [lem-trf-gordan-rational-cone-finite] to $L$ and $v_i=\overline p_i$; its monoid generated by the $v_i$ is $\overline P=\pi(P)$, and it gives the rational cone $C$ and a finite set $\overline F\subseteq C\cap L$ with $C\cap L=\bigcup_{\overline f\in\overline F}(\overline f+\overline P)$. Claim: $g\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ if and only if $\overline g\in C$. If $\overline g=\sum_i q_iv_i$ with $q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$, let $n>0$ be a common denominator of the $q_i$; then $n\overline g=\sum_i(nq_i)v_i=\overline p$ with $p=\sum_i(nq_i)p_i\in P$, so $ng-p\in T$ and $m(ng-p)=0$, i.e. $(mn)g=mp\in P$. Conversely, if $ng=\sum_i n_ip_i\in P$ with $n>0$, then $\overline g=\sum_i(n_i/n)v_i\in C$ in $L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, $L$ being free so that $L\to L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ is injective. Thus $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\pi^{-1}(C\cap L)$. For each $\overline f\in\overline F$ choose $f\in G$ with $\pi(f)=\overline f$ and put $F=\{f+t:\overline f\in\overline F,\ t\in T\}$, a finite set contained in $\pi^{-1}(C\cap L)=P^{\mathrm{sat}}$. If $g\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$, then $\overline g=\overline f+\overline p$ for some $\overline f\in\overline F$ and $p\in P$, so $t=g-f-p\in T$ and $g=(f+t)+p$ with $f+t\in F$. Conversely $F+P\subseteq P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ because $P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is closed under addition (if $ag,bh\in P$ then $ab(g+h)\in P$). Hence $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9, proof, printed p. 104; finite toric saturation, with the torsion reduction and parallelepiped argument written out.

proof.text: The inclusion $P\subseteq P^{\mathrm{sat}}\subseteq G$ and the finite translate set in Step 1 show that $P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is finitely generated and that its group completion is $G$, because $P$ already generates $G$. It is integral because it is a submonoid of the group $G$. It is saturated by definition: if $ng\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ for $n>0$, then some $mng\in P$, hence $g\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101; definition of saturation and its elementary closure properties.

proof.text: For a submonoid $S\subseteq P$, if $x\in(P-S)^{\mathrm{sat}}$, choose $n>0$ and $p\in P,s\in S$ with $nx=p-s$. Then $n(x+s)=p+(n-1)s\in P$, so $x+s\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ and $x\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}-S$. Conversely, if $x=a-s$ with $a\in P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ and $s\in S$, choose $n>0$ with $na\in P$; then $nx=na-ns\in P-S$. Hence $(P-S)^{\mathrm{sat}}=P^{\mathrm{sat}}-S$ inside $G$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101; compatibility of saturation with localization, with both inclusions written explicitly.

proof.text: Every element of the monoid algebra $R[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is a finite $R$-linear combination of basis monomials $z^g$. By Step 1, write $g=f+p$ with $f\in F$ and $p\in P$, so $z^g=z^f z^p$. Therefore the finitely many monomials $z^f$ for $f\in F$ generate $R[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ as an $R[P]$-module.

lean.statement: theorem fine_monoid_finite_saturation (P : Type u) [AddCommMonoid P] [AddMonoid.FG P] (hP : Function.Injective (GrothendieckAddGroup.of (M := P))) : ∃ Q : AddSubmonoid (GrothendieckAddGroup P), (∀ g : GrothendieckAddGroup P, g ∈ Q ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ n • g ∈ Set.range (GrothendieckAddGroup.of (M := P))) ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Multiplicative Q) ∧ (∃ e : GrothendieckAddGroup Q ≃+ GrothendieckAddGroup P, ∀ q : Q, e (GrothendieckAddGroup.of q) = q.1) ∧ (∃ F : Finset (GrothendieckAddGroup P), (∀ f ∈ F, f ∈ Q) ∧ (Q : Set (GrothendieckAddGroup P)) = ⋃ f ∈ (F : Set (GrothendieckAddGroup P)), {x | ∃ p : P, x = f + GrothendieckAddGroup.of p}) ∧ (∀ S : AddSubmonoid P, {x : GrothendieckAddGroup P | ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ p : P, ∃ s : S, n • x = GrothendieckAddGroup.of p - GrothendieckAddGroup.of s.1} = {x : GrothendieckAddGroup P | ∃ q : Q, ∃ s : S, x = q.1 - GrothendieckAddGroup.of s.1}) ∧ (∃ i : P →+ Q, (∀ p : P, (i p).1 = GrothendieckAddGroup.of p) ∧ ∀ (R : Type v) [CommRing R], (AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom R i).Finite)
